REC_J01.text: Java supports object-oriented principles including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism through class hierarchies.

REC_J02.text: Java classes can implement multiple interfaces but extend only one abstract superclass, enabling flexible type contracts.

REC_J03.text: Method overriding in Java allows a subclass to define a specialized version of an inherited method via runtime dispatch.

REC_J04.text: Java garbage collector automatically deallocates heap memory occupied by unreferenced objects using generational collection.

REC_J05.text: Abstract classes in Java cannot be instantiated directly and define common contracts enforced on all concrete subclasses.

REC_J06.text: Java Generics provide compile-time type safety by allowing classes and methods to operate on parameterized types.

REC_J07.text: Java interfaces support default method implementations since Java 8, enabling backwards-compatible API evolution without breaking existing code.

REC_J08.text: Java heap memory is partitioned into Young and Old Generation regions, with minor GC cycles targeting short-lived objects.

REC_M01.text: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors characterize invariant directional vectors under linear matrix transformations, fundamental to PCA and spectral decomposition.

REC_M02.text: Singular Value Decomposition factors any real matrix into left-singular, singular values, and right-singular matrices for low-rank approximation.

REC_M03.text: The inner dot product computes vector projection and normalizes to cosine similarity in high-dimensional metric spaces.

REC_M04.text: Matrix multiplication is associative and distributes over addition but is strictly non-commutative in general rectangular cases.

REC_M05.text: Principal Component Analysis projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal principal axes that maximize explained variance.

REC_M06.text: Matrix determinants quantify the signed scaling factor of a linear transformation on the volume spanned by its column vectors.

REC_V01.text: FAISS provides fast approximate nearest neighbor search using inverted file index and product quantization techniques.

REC_V02.text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs (HNSW) offer logarithmic time complexity for dense vector similarity retrieval.

REC_V03.text: Cosine distance and Euclidean L2 distance are the standard metrics for comparing dense vector embeddings in semantic search.

REC_V04.text: Vector databases index high-dimensional embeddings generated by transformer encoder models for semantic retrieval.

REC_V05.text: Inverted file index with flat quantization partitions vector space into Voronoi cells to accelerate approximate nearest neighbor search.

REC_V11.text: HNSW builds a multi-layer proximity graph where upper layers provide coarse navigation and lower layers enable precise nearest neighbor search.

REC_V12.text: Annoy uses random projection trees to partition vector space for memory-efficient approximate nearest neighbor similarity search.

REC_V06.text: Dense vector retrieval systems utilize approximate nearest neighbor algorithms to compare query embeddings against stored document vectors.

REC_V07.text: HNSW index structures enable scalable semantic search across millions of dense embedding vectors in sub-linear query time.

REC_V08.text: Product Quantization compresses dense vector representations by encoding subvectors into codebook centroids, reducing memory in large-scale search.

REC_V09.text: Dense vector retrieval compares high-dimensional semantic vectors using cosine similarity and angular distance thresholds for ranking.

REC_V10.text: Vector similarity search engines query dense embedding vectors generated by sentence encoder neural models against indexed corpora.

REC_V13.text: Re-ranking pipelines apply cross-encoder models on top of bi-encoder ANN retrieval to improve precision on the final result set.

REC_V14.text: Bi-encoder models independently encode query and document into fixed-length vectors enabling precomputed offline indexing for fast retrieval.

REC_P01.text: NumPy provides ndarray objects for efficient multi-dimensional vector and matrix computations in Python with C-speed performance.

REC_P02.text: Pandas DataFrames support tabular data manipulation including filtering, aggregation, groupby, merge, and time-series resampling.

REC_P03.text: Polars is an ultra-fast columnar DataFrame library implemented in Rust with a Python API, outperforming Pandas on large datasets.

REC_P04.text: Vectorized operations in NumPy eliminate explicit Python loops, providing substantial performance acceleration for array computations.

REC_P05.text: NumPy universal functions (ufuncs) apply element-wise mathematical operations across arrays with broadcasting rules for shape compatibility.

REC_P06.text: Pandas read_csv and to_parquet functions handle columnar data ingestion and serialization for efficient DataFrame storage and retrieval.

REC_P07.text: Pandas groupby with aggregate functions like sum, mean, and count enables split-apply-combine analytics on tabular datasets.

REC_P08.text: NumPy linalg module provides linear algebra routines including matrix inversion, least-squares solvers, and eigenvalue decomposition.

REC_ML01.text: PyTorch tensors support automatic differentiation via autograd for gradient-based neural network training and optimization.

REC_ML02.text: Cross-entropy loss measures the discrepancy between predicted probability distributions and true categorical labels in classification.

REC_ML03.text: Adam optimizer dynamically adapts per-parameter learning rates using first and second momentum estimates of gradient history.

REC_ML04.text: PyTorch DataLoaders handle batching, shuffling, and multi-threaded data prefetching from datasets for efficient model training.

REC_ML05.text: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to all model parameters via reverse-mode automatic differentiation.

REC_ML06.text: Dropout regularization randomly deactivates a fraction of neural connections during training to prevent overfitting on small datasets.

REC_ML07.text: Learning rate schedulers in PyTorch dynamically reduce the step size during training to stabilize convergence near loss minima.

REC_ML08.text: Batch normalization standardizes intermediate layer activations during training to reduce internal covariate shift and accelerate convergence.

REC_DB01.text: Relational databases enforce ACID guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability for reliable transaction processing.

REC_DB02.text: B-Tree indexes provide logarithmic time complexity for equality and range query lookups in relational database tables.

REC_DB03.text: Database normalization organizes schema tables into normal forms to minimize data redundancy and eliminate update anomalies.

REC_DB04.text: SQL JOIN operations combine rows from two or more tables based on related key columns to query across relationships.

REC_DB05.text: Foreign key constraints preserve referential integrity between child and parent tables by preventing orphaned records in SQL schemas.

REC_DB06.text: Write-Ahead Logging ensures committed database transactions can be fully recovered after power failures or unexpected crashes.

REC_DB07.text: PostgreSQL query execution plans show whether the optimizer uses sequential scan, index scan, or bitmap scan for each relation.

REC_DB08.text: Connection pooling via PgBouncer reduces overhead of establishing new PostgreSQL connections under high concurrency workloads.

REC_DS01.text: The CAP theorem states a distributed data store can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance simultaneously.

REC_DS02.text: Raft consensus algorithm selects a leader node to manage replicated log state machines across distributed cluster nodes via heartbeat.

REC_DS03.text: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when distributed cache nodes are dynamically added or removed from the ring.

REC_DS04.text: Two-Phase Commit coordinates atomic transaction commits across autonomous distributed database nodes with a prepare-then-commit protocol.

REC_DS05.text: Gossip protocols disseminate membership and state changes across large peer-to-peer networks with eventual consistency guarantees.

REC_DS06.text: Vector clocks track causality and detect concurrent conflicting updates in distributed key-value storage systems across replicas.

REC_DS07.text: Paxos is a consensus protocol that guarantees agreement among a quorum of distributed nodes despite minority node failures.

REC_DS08.text: Eventual consistency allows distributed replicas to temporarily diverge and converge asynchronously, prioritizing availability over immediate consistency.
